{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of the Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement (we act for the Issuer/Depositor side; Cellco acts as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian)

---

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Overall, the document is materially favourable to us. The counterparty-side indemnity in Section 6.3 is uncapped and there is no reverse indemnity from the Issuer or Depositor; the audit and inspection rights all run against Cellco rather than against us; and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-commitment, auto-renewal or customer-payable liquidated damages or penalty anywhere in the document. Assignment is symmetric with appropriate successor and affiliate carve-outs, governing law and venue are New York, and the transition regime in Section 7.5 is better than our preferred position because the outgoing Servicer bears transition costs.

Four items require attention. Two are deviations that we regard as walk-away territory as drafted: (i) Section 7.5(b) expressly relieves Cellco of any obligation to license or assign its servicing processes, models, software or applications to the Issuer or a Successor Servicer, leaving us with no right to use the platform that actually runs servicing; and (ii) the Section 6.2(a) exculpation is one-sided — Cellco is liable "only" for willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, while the mirror provision for our Depositor in Section 5.2(a) omits "only" — which is capable of excusing ordinary breach of the Servicer's core deposit, acquisition and remittance obligations. Separately, there is no customer termination-for-convenience right in an agreement that runs until the last Receivable is paid, and the Agreement contains no insurance covenant at all notwithstanding that Cellco holds Receivable Files and Personally Identifiable Information as Custodian.

One item, ownership of deliverables and Customer Data (IP), could not be completed by the automated review and requires manual attention before we sign off.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent (Section 6.3) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Needs review** | — (review incomplete) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Section 7.5(b)) |
| High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability (cap, mutuality, carve-outs) | **Deviation** | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent (Section 6.2(a)) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Sections 7.1–7.3) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous (Section 10.2) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § IX Other Agreements |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables (Sections 3.6, 3.9(e)) |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous (Sections 10.5–10.6) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | A-36 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments/volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Transfer and Acquisition of Depositor Transferred Property |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § VIII Termination |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Section 7.5) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables (Sections 3.2, 3.3, 2.5) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § III Servicing of Receivables (no covenant in document) |

---

## Walk-away items

The following two findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signing:

1. **Servicing-platform licence (Section 7.5(b)).** The clause expressly relieves Cellco of any obligation to provide, license or assign its servicing processes, models, software or applications to the Issuer or any Successor Servicer, with no path to add our affiliates, contractors or a Successor Servicer. Section 7.5(a) cooperation does not cure this, because cooperation confers no right to use the platform. **Our redline** inserts a narrow non-exclusive licence extending to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, transferable to a subsequent Successor Servicer, revocable only for uncured material breach, limited to servicing the Receivables and expressly subject to the Servicer's legal and third-party restrictions so that the existing confidentiality, privacy and data protection carve-outs are preserved.

2. **One-sided exculpation (Section 6.2(a)).** Cellco is liable "only" for willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence while the mirror provision for our Depositor at Section 5.2(a) omits "only", and the blanket waiver of "All other liability" is capable of excusing ordinary breach of the Servicer Deposit Obligation, the Servicer Acquisition Obligation and remittance of Collections — our principal recourse. The Section 6.3 indemnities are triggered by the same narrow standard. **Our redline** is minimal: delete "only" to restore symmetry with Section 5.2(a) and confirm that the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's specific obligations (deposit, acquisition and indemnity) sit outside any limitation on liability. We are not seeking a monetary cap — there is none today, and the absence of a cap favours us as claimant; a Servicing Fee-based cap would be illusory.

---

## Next steps

1. **Complete the IP review.** The ownership of deliverables and Customer Data analysis failed in processing and must be completed manually before we clear the document. This is a critical-severity rule and we should not sign off without it.
2. **Issue the two walk-away redlines** described above (Sections 7.5(b) and 6.2(a)) as priority items, with the rationale and fallback framing set out in each comment.
3. **Add a customer convenience exit.** There is no Issuer right to remove the Servicer other than for a Servicer Termination Event under Section 7.2(c), and the Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full or the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.3 — well beyond 12 months. The Article VIII optional acquisition and redemption rights sit with the Class A Certificateholder (the Originators or their designee), so they are not a customer exit. We propose a 30-day, no-fee convenience termination right, conditioned on a Successor Servicer accepting engagement under Section 7.4 to preserve servicing continuity for the Noteholders. Note the counterparty side is already better than our preferred position: Section 7.1 bars Cellco from resigning except where legally unable to perform.
4. **Insert an insurance covenant.** We propose a new Section 10.14 in Article X requiring Cellco, in all three of its capacities, to carry CGL (USD 1M/2M), E&O (USD 2M), cyber (USD 5M) and workers' compensation as required by law, with certificates on request, given that Cellco holds and maintains the Receivable Files and Personally Identifiable Information as Custodian and Exhibit A (Custodian's Security Requirements) is not reproduced in this form. Insurance covenants are atypical in a transfer and servicing agreement of this type and Section 6.3 provides some overlapping protection, so this is a low-severity ask; the fallback of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment if the full programme is resisted.
5. **Low-priority comment only.** Under Section 7.5(b), file and record delivery is "as soon as practicable" rather than subject to a hard outside date; we would raise a 30-day delivery deadline as a non-blocking comment. We also note, without redlining, that the Section 10.6 jurisdiction grant is nonexclusive (which preserves our ability to sue elsewhere) and that Section 6.3 has no IP-infringement limb (immaterial here, as there are no vendor deliverables or IP grant).
6. **Confirm Exhibit A.** Request the Custodian's Security Requirements exhibit, which is not reproduced in the form we reviewed, and review it against the insurance and data-handling positions above."}
